topic.title: Payments idempotency — surviving retries without double-charging
topic.concept: Networks retry and clients double-click; idempotency makes the retried operation return the ORIGINAL result instead of executing twice. It is the load-bearing wall of payment APIs.
points: Client sends an Idempotency-Key header (UUID); server stores key → response for a TTL (Stripe: 24h) and replays the stored response on repeats.
The key check and the write must be atomic — unique constraint on the key column, INSERT first, act second; check-then-act races under concurrency.
In-flight duplicate (same key, first still processing) → 409 or wait; different body with same key → 422, never silent reuse.
At-least-once delivery downstream (queues) needs consumer-side dedupe: processed-message table or exactly-once semantics (Kafka transactions).
Outbox pattern: write business row + event in ONE DB transaction; a relay publishes — avoids the dual-write inconsistency between DB and broker.
topic.angle: 'A payment request timed out — the client retries. What happens in your design?' Strong answers walk the exact key lifecycle (miss, in-flight, replay) and name where atomicity comes from.
